front_blocks.md: Define **closed circulatory system**.

back_blocks.md: In a **closed circulatory system**, blood is always contained within **blood vessels** and the heart, and does not directly bathe the tissues.

cards.front_md: Define **closed circulatory system**.

front_blocks.md: Define **double circulation**.

back_blocks.md: In a **double circulation**, blood passes through the **heart twice** for each complete circuit of the body.

cards.front_md: Define **double circulation**.
cards.back_md: In a **double circulation**, blood passes through the **heart twice** for each complete circuit of the body.

front_blocks.md: Name the **two circuits** of the mammalian double circulation.

back_blocks.md: The **pulmonary circulation** — between the heart and the lungs.
The **systemic circulation** — between the heart and the rest of the body.

cards.front_md: Name the **two circuits** of the mammalian double circulation.
cards.back_md:
The **pulmonary circulation** — between the heart and the lungs.

The **systemic circulation** — between the heart and the rest of the body.

front_blocks.md: List the **five types of blood vessel** blood flows through, in order away from the heart.

back_blocks.md: **Arteries** → **arterioles** → **capillaries** → **venules** → **veins**.

cards.front_md: List the **five types of blood vessel** blood flows through, in order away from the heart.

front_blocks.md: What is the function of the **pulmonary artery**?

back_blocks.md: It carries **deoxygenated** blood from the heart (right ventricle) to the **lungs**.

cards.front_md: What is the function of the **pulmonary artery**?
cards.back_md: It carries **deoxygenated** blood from the heart (right ventricle) to the **lungs**.

front_blocks.md: What is the function of the **pulmonary vein**?

back_blocks.md: It carries **oxygenated** blood from the **lungs** back to the heart (left atrium).

cards.front_md: What is the function of the **pulmonary vein**?
cards.back_md: It carries **oxygenated** blood from the **lungs** back to the heart (left atrium).

front_blocks.md: What is the function of the **aorta**?

back_blocks.md: It carries **oxygenated** blood from the heart (left ventricle) to the **body**.

cards.front_md: What is the function of the **aorta**?
cards.back_md: It carries **oxygenated** blood from the heart (left ventricle) to the **body**.

front_blocks.md: What is the function of the **vena cava**?

back_blocks.md: It carries **deoxygenated** blood from the **body** back to the heart (right atrium).

cards.front_md: What is the function of the **vena cava**?
cards.back_md: It carries **deoxygenated** blood from the **body** back to the heart (right atrium).

front_blocks.md: Which two vessels make up the **pulmonary circulation**?

back_blocks.md: The **pulmonary artery** (heart → lungs) and the **pulmonary vein** (lungs → heart).

cards.front_md: Which two vessels make up the **pulmonary circulation**?

front_blocks.md: How can you recognise an **artery** in a transverse section?

back_blocks.md: It has a **thick wall** and a relatively **small, round lumen**, often with a folded (wavy) inner lining.

front_blocks.md: How can you recognise a **capillary**?

back_blocks.md: It has a **wall one cell thick** and a lumen just wide enough for a single **red blood cell**.

front_blocks.md: Define a **plan diagram**.

back_blocks.md: A **plan diagram** is a low-power drawing showing the **outlines of tissues**, with no individual cells drawn.

front_blocks.md: In which two planes can a blood vessel be **sectioned** to draw a plan diagram?

back_blocks.md: **Transverse section (TS)** — a cross-section across the vessel.

front_blocks.md: How is the structure of an **elastic artery** related to its function?

back_blocks.md: Its wall contains much **elastic tissue** that **stretches and recoils**.
This smooths out the high-pressure surges from the heart, maintaining a steadier blood flow.

cards.front_md: How is the structure of an **elastic artery** related to its function?
cards.back_md:
Its wall contains much **elastic tissue** that **stretches and recoils**.

This smooths out the high-pressure surges from the heart, maintaining a steadier blood flow.

front_blocks.md: How is the structure of a **muscular artery** related to its function?

back_blocks.md: Its wall contains **smooth muscle** that contracts and relaxes.
This controls the volume of blood distributed to different organs.

front_blocks.md: How is the structure of a **vein** related to its function?

back_blocks.md: It has a **thin wall**, a **wide lumen** and **valves**.
This returns blood to the heart at low pressure, with the valves preventing backflow.

front_blocks.md: How is the structure of a **capillary** related to its function?

back_blocks.md: Its wall is only **one cell thick**, giving a **short diffusion distance**.
This allows efficient exchange of substances between the blood and tissues.

back_blocks.md: The **endothelium** is the smooth, single layer of cells that **lines** all blood vessels, reducing friction with the blood.

front_blocks.md: How does the **solvent action** of water help transport in mammals?

back_blocks.md: Many substances (such as glucose, ions and oxygen) **dissolve** in water.
This allows them to be carried in solution in the blood plasma.

cards.front_md: How does the **solvent action** of water help transport in mammals?
cards.back_md:
Many substances (such as glucose, ions and oxygen) **dissolve** in water.

This allows them to be carried in solution in the blood plasma.

front_blocks.md: How does the **high specific heat capacity** of water help mammals?

back_blocks.md: Water **resists changes in temperature**.
This lets the blood distribute heat around the body and helps keep body temperature stable.

cards.front_md: How does the **high specific heat capacity** of water help mammals?

Water **resists changes in temperature**.

front_blocks.md: Define **specific heat capacity**.

back_blocks.md: **Specific heat capacity** is the energy needed to raise the temperature of a substance by a given amount; water's is **high**, so it warms and cools slowly.

front_blocks.md: Define **tissue fluid**.

back_blocks.md: **Tissue fluid** is the fluid that surrounds and bathes the body's cells, formed from **blood plasma**.

cards.front_md: Define **tissue fluid**.
cards.back_md: **Tissue fluid** is the fluid that surrounds and bathes the body's cells, formed from **blood plasma**.

front_blocks.md: State the **functions of tissue fluid**.

back_blocks.md: It supplies cells with **oxygen, glucose and other nutrients**.
It removes **waste products** (such as carbon dioxide) from cells.
It acts as the medium of exchange between the blood and the cells.

cards.front_md: State the **functions of tissue fluid**.
cards.back_md:
It supplies cells with **oxygen, glucose and other nutrients**.

It removes **waste products** (such as carbon dioxide) from cells.

It acts as the medium of exchange between the blood and the cells.

front_blocks.md: How is tissue fluid **formed** at the arterial end of a capillary?

back_blocks.md: The high **hydrostatic pressure** forces plasma (without large proteins and cells) out through the capillary wall.
This is called **ultrafiltration**.

cards.front_md: How is tissue fluid **formed** at the arterial end of a capillary?
cards.back_md:
The high **hydrostatic pressure** forces plasma (without large proteins and cells) out through the capillary wall.

This is called **ultrafiltration**.

front_blocks.md: Why does water **return** to the capillary at the venous end?

back_blocks.md: Hydrostatic pressure has fallen, and the remaining **plasma proteins** give the blood a **low water potential**.
So water re-enters the capillary by **osmosis**.
